dbp.description:
Everyone will have a seat at the table in the biggest, ongoing digital art collaboration. This is Async Art's first Dynamic Blueprint collection, a homage to First Supper, the world's first programmable, dynamic NFT that was minted in 2020. 

Everyone starts with an empty room. Over time Async artists and team will release different backgrounds, decor, and characters called Expansion Packs for collectors to pick and decorate their room with. How you customize your room is entirely up to you. 

Make it your story.

itemCache.name: Clara Tice
itemCache.description:
Clara was an artist and illustrator, with her drawings featuring in Vanity Fair.

Notably, a cafe was raided by the New York Society for the Suppression of Vice - the morality police - in search of her artworks, which caused demand for her art to skyrocket.

itemCache.name: Queen of Greenwich Village
itemCache.description:
Clara had a style and fashion all of her own.

Some say that she invented the 'bob' haircut popular during the 1920s.

itemCache.name: Baroness Elsa von Freytag-Loringhoven
itemCache.description: Elsa could often be found wearing anything from dangling spoons to  feathers, or indeed hardly anything at all - nudity was a crime for which she was arrested multiple times.

itemCache.name: R. Mutt
itemCache.description: Some have conjectured that it was Elsa herself who came up with the idea of Duchamp’s famous urinal, and sent it to him signed R. Mutt.

itemCache.name: Beatrice Wood
itemCache.description:
Beatrice Wood famously remarked to Marcel Duchamp that 'anyone could do modern art' - and so when he replied to her to go do it, she did.

She presented two paintings at two paintings at the first exhibition of the Society of Independent Artists, in 1917.

itemCache.name: The Blind Man
itemCache.description: Beatrice founded, along with Duchamp and Henri-Pierre Roché, the Dada magazine 'The Blind Man' which published art and text from the avante garde in New York City.

itemCache.name: Suzanne Duchamp
itemCache.description: Suzanne will always be known as "the sister of Marcel" and yet was an artist herself and was included in the Salon des Indípendants in 1920, the first Dada exhibition in Paris.

itemCache.name: Un et une menacés
itemCache.description: A 1916 collage by Suzanne Duchamp of a couple destined to never connect.

itemCache.name: Hannah Höch
itemCache.description:
Hannah was a pioneer of photomontage and used commerical images to produce polital satire.

She also used her art to promote women's sufferage and as a means of rebellion against the commercialised image of the feminine.

itemCache.name: The Painter
itemCache.description: This the title of Hannah Höch's short story about a husband who experiences a crisis when asked  to do the  dishes.

$inf$/dynamicBlueprints/63fe742c74e62000.description:
“Dada doubts everything,” wrote Dada founding member Tristan Tzara in 1920 & Dada remains one of the most anarchistic cultural movements of all time.

This set of figures highlights and pays homage to the women of the Dada movement.
$inf$/dynamicBlueprints/63fe742c74e62000.title: Women Of Dada

common.async-music-classic-copy-1: What is Async Music Classic? Async Music Classic is a curated gallery of 17 diverse & interactive music pieces created by the early innovators in web3 music between April 2021 and February 2022. Interactive music consist of compositions with the ability to change their parameters; the songs in this gallery may sound different each time you come back to listen. This is achieved by breaking down a song into separate layers called Stems. Each Stem has multiple Variants for its new owner to choose from. In this way, a single Async Music Classic track contains many unique combinations of sounds.
